canDo: Can write a forum contribution of 250+ words with a clear position on a controversial topic: respond to the previous contributor, concede before rebutting, organise 2–3 arguments with connectors and give concrete examples.
review: Review discourse connectors (d’abord / ensuite / enfin, d’une part… d’autre part, quant à, en définitive) and concession (certes… mais, bien que + subjunctive, même si, sans pour autant); build on day 32’s “identify the author’s position” reading practice: today you state your own.
input: Read: an analysis of “digital detox”, a column arguing “stop making users feel guilty” and a forum post in which parents share a “no smartphone before the end of middle school” pact; listen: a radio debate on a minimum age for social media, an interview about a company blocking emails in the evening and an announcement for a media library’s digital workshops.
output: Write: a forum contribution of 250+ words on “Should under-16s be banned from social media?” (respond at the start, concede then rebut, at least 5 different connectors, a summing-up at the end); speak: a 6-minute monologue on “a screen-free week at secondary school”, then debate “fully digital administrative procedures” with the examiner.
checkpoint: The forum contribution reaches 250 words, with a clear position statement, 1 response to someone else’s view, 2 concessive structures and 5+ different connectors; self-check against the 6 criteria of the official marking grid with no obvious gaps.
challenge: Today’s challenge: find a news item about screens, social media or artificial intelligence on TV5MONDE or RFI’s « Journal en français facile » and write 5 sentences as if replying on a forum: concede first with « Certes… », then state your position with « Toutefois / Quant à… / En définitive… ».

questions.why: The question at the end of the first paragraph, « Faut-il y voir une mode passagère ou le signe d’un malaise plus profond ? », is the thread of the whole text; it then analyses causes, effects, and the effects and limits of detox. A: nothing is being sold; C is too definite: the third paragraph says researchers are cautious and causality is unclear.

« Ce réflexe n’est pas le fruit du hasard : de nombreuses applications sont conçues pour retenir l’utilisateur ». B contradicts « souvent sans raison précise »; C is the “individual responsibility” view the article questions at the end.
The text explains it straight after: « plus nous restons connectés, plus les plateformes vendent d’espaces publicitaires ». A and B both misread économie literally as “saving”.
« il est difficile de savoir si les écrans provoquent ces troubles ou si les personnes déjà fragiles s’y réfugient davantage »: the direction of causality is unclear. Neither A nor C is mentioned.
« mieux vaut modifier durablement quelques usages… que viser une abstinence totale ». B: he thinks a week without a phone « ne change rien »; C is the “total abstinence” he rejects.

Enfin introduces a criticism of the very idea of “detox”, and En définitive shifts the issue to “designing tools that serve us”. A is wrong: the testimonies come earlier; C: there is no ban in the text.

« c’est bien la conception des outils qu’il faudrait encadrer » and the ending, « exiger des outils qui ne nous intoxiquent pas ». A is exactly the line the author criticises; B: he only proposes banning “infinite scroll” for minors, not phones.

A tired individual will versus design by teams of engineers: « lutter seul contre le courant » is a metaphor for an uneven fight. B is a literal misreading; C is the opposite of what the metaphor means.
« D’autre part, et c’est plus grave, il détourne le regard des vrais responsables »; d’une part… d’autre part lists two points, and c’est plus grave marks the more serious one. A and C have no basis.

« imposer la ceinture de sécurité… sans pour autant interdire la voiture », used to rebut « la loi ne peut pas tout ». B is the view the author concedes and then overturns; A: no comparison is intended.
détox / intoxiquent is a play on words, and the imperative commençons par exiger makes a forceful ending. B and C don’t fit the author’s combative stance.

Signed Fabien_P, written in the first person (« un bilan : le voici ») and ending with an invitation to ask questions, it is a parent sharing a group initiative on a forum. B and C don’t fit the genre.

« Chaque parent finissait par céder parce que “tous les autres en ont un”… En nous engageant ensemble… personne n’est le seul à dire non ». A isn’t mentioned; C contradicts the fact that his daughter was angry at first.
« reconnaît aujourd’hui qu’elle ne se sent pas exclue, puisque ses amies sont dans le même cas ». A: it was two families who dropped out; B contrasts with « au début », showing things have changed.
« sans messagerie de groupe, organiser un après-midi au parc demande plusieurs coups de fil ». Neither B nor C is mentioned.
The host opens with: « interdire les réseaux sociaux aux moins de quinze ans. Bonne idée ou fausse solution ? ». A confuses it with “banning phones at school”; C is proposed by no one.
« des conflits qui ont commencé en ligne… ils continuent le soir, la nuit, le week-end ». B and C aren’t mentioned.
« Ensuite, pour la rendre efficace, il faudrait vérifier l’identité de tous les utilisateurs… Cela porterait gravement atteinte à la vie privée ». “Easy to get round” is his first argument.
« on ne renonce pas à une règle simplement parce qu’elle sera parfois contournée. L’alcool est interdit aux mineurs, et pourtant certains en boivent »: it rebuts the “easy to get round” argument.

« Elle a raison, la loi peut aider les parents, je l’admets ». B is exactly the logic he criticises (« ne devient pas inoffensif le jour des quinze ans »); C: he is actually calling for more media education.
« qu’on impose aux plateformes des règles strictes pour tous les mineurs, et qu’on développe l’éducation aux médias à l’école ». Neither A nor C is what he proposes.
« les courriels ne sont plus distribués entre vingt heures et sept heures du matin ». B goes too far; C: it’s an internal company measure, not a law.
« beaucoup se sentaient obligés de répondre immédiatement, de peur de passer pour peu motivés ». A and C aren’t mentioned.

« avaient l’impression d’être infantilisés… des parents qui préfèrent partir tôt… et terminer leur travail le soir »: they lost the freedom to organise their own time. A is the opposite of how it works (emails are still delivered in the morning).
Sick leave fell “slightly”, but « il est difficile d’affirmer que c’est uniquement grâce à cette mesure », and « la technique ne règle pas tout ». A ignores the reservation; C contradicts the data.

The opening questions, « Vous êtes mal à l’aise avec Internet ? Vous avez du mal à faire vos démarches en ligne… ? », make the target audience clear. B is mentioned only at the end, as potential volunteers.

« en petits groupes de six personnes au maximum » and « Inutile d’avoir un ordinateur : du matériel sera prêté sur place ». A is the opposite; C: there are only Tuesday and Thursday sessions (plus Saturdays by appointment).
« pourquoi ne pas devenir bénévole ? L’équipe recherche des volontaires ». A: the workshops are free; B isn’t said.

V33-01.exZh: For some, digital detox is just a passing fad.

V33-02.exZh: In the attention economy, our screen time is turned into advertising revenue.

V33-03.exZh: With infinite scroll, you never know when to stop.

V33-04.exZh: Work stress often shows up as sleep disorders.

V33-05.exZh: The little restaurant’s success is no accident.

V33-06.zh: hard to dispute, all but undeniable
V33-06.exZh: This figure is hard to dispute: it comes from three independent studies.

V33-07.exZh: Before banning screens at the table for children, parents have to lead by example.

V33-08.exZh: Ultimately, the problem lies in how the tool is used, not the tool itself.

V33-09.exZh: This kind of talk makes parents who finish work late feel guilty.

V33-10.exZh: Rather than blaming users, we should regulate the platforms.

V33-11.exZh: You can limit notifications without necessarily giving up social media.

V33-12.zh: not to be able to do everything
V33-12.exZh: Schools can’t do everything; families have a role to play too.

V33-13.exZh: I understand the argument, but it doesn’t take small towns into account.

V33-14.exZh: My younger brother has been hooked on video games since last summer.

V33-15.exZh: After turning off notifications, I felt I had taken back control.

V33-16.exZh: All it takes to get round the ban is to lie about your age.

V33-17.zh: to have one’s eyes glued to
V33-17.exZh: He crossed the street with his eyes glued to his phone.

V33-18.exZh: Without an account on this network, some students feel left out of conversations.

V33-19.zh: to take refuge in, to seek comfort in
V33-19.exZh: After his failure, he took refuge in video games.

V33-20.exZh: Every spring, you have to declare your income online.

V33-21.exZh: The media library offers one-to-one support on Saturday mornings.

V33-22.zh: to be uncomfortable with, not at ease with
V33-22.exZh: Many older people aren’t at ease with online forms.

V33-23.exZh: Platforms must comply with these rules or, where applicable, pay a fine.

V33-24.zh: what’s more, on top of that
V33-24.exZh: The measure doesn’t work, and what’s more, it’s very expensive.

V33-25.exZh: With parental controls, apps are locked after 22:00.
